newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end lower as Brazil volatility looms.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end lower as Brazil volatility looms.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended sharply lower on Friday amid persistent concerns over recent volatility on the Brazilian equity markets.

"The Brazil situation is still delicate, and players see that as increasing risks of a short-term capital outflow in the region," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
Mexico's blue-chip IPC index ended down 95.81 points, or 1.99 percent, at 4,720.56. In Sao Paulo, the Bovespa index of most active stocks lost 547 points, or 4.66 percent to 11,182.
"Brazil has been volatile for a few days now, and that inevitably heightens concern," Rojas added.
"In a situation like this, dealers prefer to call their opponents' hand and go liquid," a desk trader said.

"Our fundamentals are still sound, so this has to be a passing phase. But even so dealers use it as a pretext to take profits before stepping back in. At the end of the day, we're still part of Latin America," he added.
Traders said moderate trading volume of 83.7 million shares signalled that investors may not have jumped out of Mexico.
Dealers said profit-taking on Wall Street also influenced activity on the Mexican bourse, but to a lesser extent than Brazil. The Dow Jones industrial average ended down 130.31 points at 7,890.46.

Traders said Brazil's long shadow was most notable in the case of Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex). Its shares fell in step with Brazil's Telebras, which swooned amid concern over the impact of a possible rate cut in August.
In New York, Telmex American Depositary Receipts finished 1-9/16 lower at 50-5/16, outpacing the broader market's decline.
Financial firm Bancomer lost 10 centavos (1 cent) to 4.50 pesos (57 cents) at brisk trade.
Traders said the stock fell victim to rising secondary interest rates, which tend to increase past-due loans problems.

Kimberly Clark de Mexico SA de CV, a paper company in which Kimberly Clark Corp. of the United States has a minority stake, ended near the top of the table of prominent decliners. The stock fell 2.80 pesos (35 cents) to 32.10 pesos ($4.06) after posting second-quarter earnings on Thursday that analysts said were disappointing.
On the broad market, decliners far outnumbered gainers by 72 to 23 amid a total of 111 stocks traded.
